originality.rationale: The candidate is an exact finite two-window collision second-moment law and a positive-order asymptotic variance for random cyclic 2-binomial type diversity. The own published deterministic theorem establishes the observable and sharp bounds but neither the joint balanced-window enumeration nor its random moments. Rao–Rigo–Salimov study avoidance, Golafshan counts global linear equivalence classes, Arnoux studies contiguous circular factors, and OEIS A119462 counts adjacent cyclic 01 factors. An unindexed exact local-time equivalent is a genuine residual risk.
residual_risks: The second moment of balanced semicircle windows could exist under a different name in local-time or circular scan-statistics literature; search cannot establish uniqueness.
An inaccessible full text on circular factors was assessed only from its abstract; no whole-document NOT_COVERING assertion is made.

A general hypergeometric pair-collision identity may appear in specialized statistics sources; the original claim is its exact cyclic-signature interpretation with variance constant, not the generic hypergeometric identity.

value.rationale: The arithmetic gcd=2 stratum is the first in which cyclic 2-binomial fingerprints can collide. The exact joint-window formula and its positive leading variance distinguish typical orbital signature diversity from existing sharp extremal bounds. A nonzero order-m variance is a substantive fluctuation statement on an infinite natural fixed-composition family, providing quantitative structure needed for random cyclic signature diversity studies; it is not a new extremal bound or an arbitrary finite slice.
